scenario.prompt:
Course title: World Literature Survey
Build an 8-week undergraduate survey for first-year students. Include close reading of The Epic of Gilgamesh, The Odyssey, Antigone, selected poems by Li Bai and Du Fu, The Thousand and One Nights, Dante’s Inferno, Things Fall Apart, and Borges’s “The Library of Babel.” Students should analyze narrative structure, voice, imagery, historical context, translation choices, and evidence-based comparison. Use weekly passage annotations, two comparative reading responses, a comparative essay proposal, and a final comparative paper. Require locatable textual evidence, a credible counter-reading, and explicit limits on every major interpretation. Keep all readings edition-neutral and do not invent page numbers or quotations.

readingTitles: selected poems by Li Bai and Du Fu

agentAudit.question: Where do students compare The Odyssey and The Thousand and One Nights, and what textual evidence, counter-reading, and claim limit must they use?
agentAudit.answer: Comparative Reading Responses schedules the comparison between The Odyssey and The Thousand and One Nights in Lesson 2: Narrative Structure: The Odyssey, under Assignment Briefs. Students must analyze one locatable passage or formal feature from each work, make a comparative claim that needs both texts, test a credible counter-reading against the same paired evidence, revise the claim, and state explicitly what the selected passages cannot establish on their own.
